Posted: the full revised chapter two as prose (about 995 words) with the notes.

**Priya found the worst error in the book and it's fixed.** The disputed sentence has a comma after "stayed," sitting four lines above Prue declaring there is no comma in it — the narration failing the exact kind of check the chapter is built on. I took neither repair she offered: cutting the comma damages the sentence, and "the comma never moved" leaks the 10:03/10:07 reveal early. Instead I changed Hal's error. He now says the line is the last sentence of chapter nine; it's fourth from the end, with three sentences after it that Mark wrote on a Sunday and has never liked. Precise, confident, checkable, wrong, and it touches nothing the reveal depends on.

**The blind test is cut.** I told Gus last round it was first out if it dragged. He says it drags and he got bored. I think Oren is right on the merits — it was what made Mark *need* the log — but my word on that is worth more than my preference, and the ear test plus the unsent concession still carry Mark to the record.

**Em is cut**, because Gus moved to Oren's side. That collapses the trade I made last round: I paid Sid Karr to keep Em and have now lost both. I'm not asking for Sid back.

**Refused a third time:** "It is the best sentence in the book" stays. Oren has asked three rounds running; Gus reports it's what made him care whose sentence it was, and that's what the paragraph is for. I've told Oren plainly I'm not moving.

**Also taken from Oren:** Quirework's reason for keeping an unsent line is now on the page, and it's Mark's own configuration from two years earlier, "being a man who likes to know what he nearly said."

Chapter two is about 995 words against 1,400, and the book about 2,550 against roughly 3,250. I've stated that once for the record and dropped it.
